title: Throughput & tail-latency benchmarking for FP8/INT8 calibration across mixed-size batching and extended-window sessions
creator: Daniel Park
description: Goal: Measure end-to-end throughput and tail latency (p95/p99) impact when serving FP8 and INT8 calibrated variants under realistic mixed-size batching and extended-session workloads. Focus areas: calibration stability across sliding-window sessions, interactions with KV cache warmup/eviction, kernel scheduler behavior for mixed batch shapes, and accuracy regression profiling vs float32 baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Collect throughput and p50/p95/p99 latency across batching shapes [1,4,16,64] and request mixes (65% short, 25% mid, 10% extended-window).
Produce calibration artifacts for FP8 and INT8 with seed/parameters so experiments are reproducible and check into s3://redwood-quant-calib/experiments/ENG-782451/.
Identify kernel scheduler hotpaths that degrade p99 for mixed batches and propose mitigations (config flags or fallback rules).
Quantify accuracy delta (perplexity / EM / eval-sets) on the calibration holdout: flag any >1% relative drop vs FP32 and mark as candidate for per-layer fp32 fallback.
Ship a reproducible benchmark harness PR and an observations dashboard link in ticket comments.
steps: Assemble representative traffic profile from production traces (sanitized) and synthesize request sequences with short (8 tokens), mid (128 tokens), and extended-window (up to 64k tokens) conversations.
Create calibrated weight packs for FP8 and INT8 using the unified calibration pipeline (use calibration set: dev-evals/quant-holdout-2026-01, 5k examples).
Run microbenchmarks across model variants on a Dedicated cluster (A100x8) with kernel-scheduler logging enabled, measuring throughput and latency per-token and end-to-end per-request.
Run end-to-end harness with mixed-size batching and KV cache enabled to capture tail effects during KV warmup and eviction events.
Collect accuracy metrics by running the eval harness on 3 held-out eval suites (synthetic-span, codegen-smoke, and dialog-coherence).
Iterate on calibration parameters (clip thresholds, per-channel scales) for FP8 to reduce accuracy regression; log calibration configs with artifact hashes.
Open PRs for benchmark harness and an ops runbook to toggle scheduler mitigations, attach dashboards and perf traces to the ticket.
results_summary: Preliminary runs (2026-03-02) show FP8 increases steady-state token throughput by ~1.85x vs FP32 and INT8 by ~1.55x on our baseline model. For mixed-size batching the median latency improves proportional to throughput, but observed p99 regression is workload-dependent: when extended-window traffic constitutes >8% of requests, p99 increases by 18-65ms on FP8 relative to FP32, largely attributable to KV cache eviction cascades and kernel scheduler preemption. INT8 shows smaller p99 degradation (~8-25ms). Calibration tuned with per-layer clipping reduced accuracy regression to <0.6% relative on the dialog-coherence suite for FP8. Mitigation path: enable kernel-scheduler affinity for long-sequence microbatches and conservative KV eviction when session-age & batch-size indicate hot-KV; this recovers ~60% of the observed p99 delta in follow-up runs.
